header:
Date: 2026-04-21 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: zoom.us/rec/abcd1234 (internal)
Attendees: Elena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Andre Gomes (Redwood CSM); Priya Shah (Brightline Head of Platform), Tom Rivera (Brightline ML Eng), Lisa Wu (Brightline Infra), Miguel Santos (Brightline Security)
summary: Weekly pilot sync focused on onboarding progress, infra gating items, and early model quality tradeoffs. Team agreed to targeted quantization bench, share SOC2 and network diagrams, and run a short latency run for 2k token prompts. Risks: KMS/HSM decision and VPC peering timing could delay staging rollouts. Action items assigned and next steps scheduled.
transcript: [00:00] Elena Park: Hi everyone thanks for joining, we're gonna kick off. can you hear me?
[00:07] Priya Shah: Yes loud and clear. We have Tom, Lisa and Miguel on our side — thanks for coordinating Elena.

[00:15] Elena Park: Great. Quick agenda — 1) access and infra gate, 2) bench results and quant tuning, 3) security questions, and 4) next steps. Marcus will cover the bench details. Andre is here for onboarding blockers.

[00:30] Marcus Lee: Hey all. We ran the first pass with the medium size model you requested against your sample traffic — caveat the sample was trimmed. p50 is around 110ms for 256 tokens on our hosted nodes, p95 was 540ms so we want to discuss batching and prefix caching to bring that down for your tail latency goals.

[01:05] Tom Rivera: That p95 sounds promising, but our SLA target is 300ms for interactive flows. We're using a 2k token system prompt for some flows so numbers will change. Did you run the 2k token sample yet?

[01:22] Marcus Lee: Not the full 2k across all variant prompts yet — that was part of the quantization run we're proposing. The 2k pushes KV cache behavior; we expect p95 to rise and more variability. We'll run a targeted 2k bench next and include cold vs warm cache numbers.

[01:45] Lisa Wu: On infra: staging VPC peering is scheduled but there's a dependency on our networking team to approve the egress policy. If that slips we may not be able to test dedicated capacity in staging on time.
[02:05] Elena Park: Understood. Is there a blocker we can help unblock? I can pull in our infra ops if needed. Also for peering, do you need an architecture diagram or IP ranges from us?
[02:18] Lisa Wu: IP ranges would help plus an outline of the NAT traversal approach. We also need the console access roles — RBAC mapping so we can align with our SAML groups.
[02:35] Andre Gomes: I'll share the role mapping template after the call. we also have a short runbook for onboarding dedicated pools, that usually helps accelerate the peering handoff.

[02:50] Miguel Santos: On security: we looked at default key management options. we need clarity if Redwood's private offers support customer-managed KMS with HSM. If not, we may require an HSM path or a dedicated encryption boundary for PHI, otherwise procurement flags it.

[03:12] Elena Park: Good question. For our Private deploy we support CMK via major cloud KMS providers and we can integrate customer HSMs in the on-prem package — there's a short tech note we'll share. For hosted we have envelope encryption but not customer-managed HSM by default.

[03:36] Miguel Santos: OK please send the SOC2 report and the network diagram. That will go to procurement. Also need retention policy for logs and whether token-level telemetry includes prompt contents by default.

[03:55] Marcus Lee: By default telemetry is aggregated; prompt strings are redacted unless you enable detailed logging. We can set tenant-level retention and redaction rules; I'll add that detail to the security note we share.
[04:13] Priya Shah: On model quality — we saw some differences on hallucination on decision-tree style prompts. Can we test a reranking flow or smaller model variant to reduce bad outputs?

[04:30] Marcus Lee: Yes reranking is an option; another is temperature tuning plus prompt engineering and spot-checking with Redwood Optimize suggestions. For latency-sensitive flows we sometimes push a quantized variant which trims precision but usually keeps quality within an acceptable delta — we'll quantify that for your tasks.
[05:02] Tom Rivera: How do you measure "acceptable delta"? We need clear pass/fail criteria: e.g., <5% drop in semantic score on our eval set and no critical hallucinations on top-100 prompts.

[05:18] Elena Park: Good framing. If you can share the eval set we'll run those before/after quant runs and provide delta metrics and example regressions. We'll also include a few synthetic edge prompts.
[05:34] Tom Rivera: We'll upload eval_v2.csv to the shared drive after the call.

[05:40] Marcus Lee: Perfect. For quantization we'll run: fp16 baseline, 8-bit quant, and a 4-bit experiment on a small subset. Expect quality/latency tradeoffs in the results table. We'll include p50/p95/p99 and token-cost estimates.
[06:05] Priya Shah: Cost is likely a big lever for us. We want to see committed vs burst pricing for dedicated pools — can you show scenarios so finance can sign off?

[06:20] Elena Park: Yes I'll prepare a few scenarios: purely hosted, dedicated reservation x3 months, and hybrid (hosted fallback + reserved base). I'll include cost per 1M tokens and estimated monthly spend for your projected QPS.

[06:35] Lisa Wu: Also need a rollback/fallback plan if dedicated capacity is unavailable — e.g., routing to hosted with throttles and transformation rules. We can't have traffic drop during business hours.

[06:47] Marcus Lee: That's built into smart routing — policy can route by latency or by region and have automatic fallback to a compatible model variant. We'll draft a short canary playbook for you that includes step-by-step switchovers and traffic cutover metrics.
[07:05] Priya Shah: That sounds good. timeline wise, when can you run the 2k prompt p95 bench?
[07:12] Marcus Lee: We can run it tomorrow if you provide the sample. I'll need the exact prompt set and call patterns (concurrency).
[07:21] Tom Rivera: I'll upload the 2k_prompts.json and provide concurrency config — aiming for a realistic burst profile.

[07:30] Elena Park: On the action items: Marcus — quant runs and bench; Elena — pricing scenarios and SOC2/doc links; Andre — role mapping and runbook. Lisa and Miguel to confirm networking and KMS decisions. We'll recap at the end with dates.
[07:50] Miguel Santos: One more question: audit logs retention in Private vs Hosted — can you confirm max retention windows and export formats? We need CSV exports for SIEM ingestion.

[08:03] Marcus Lee: Private offers configurable retention and direct export to your S3 or syslog; hosted has a default 90-day retention with longer windows as an add-on. We'll include exact export formats in the security bundle.
[08:24] Elena Park: Quick note on telemetry — we can redact prompt content by default and maintain token-level usage metrics for billing. That solves some of the PHI concerns if you prefer redaction.
[08:40] Priya Shah: Good. We prefer redaction for initial pilot, then evaluate selective logging for debug sessions.
[08:48] Marcus Lee: Understood. We'll make redaction the default for your tenant in the pilot config.
[09:00] Priya Shah: Anything else on infra?
[09:03] Lisa Wu: I'll confirm egress limits and get back by Friday with exact timings. If egress needs to be enlarged that could add a 3 day change window but not a hard blocker.
[09:18] Elena Park: Great. Let's go through the recap and explicit next steps — Marcus can you call out the bench deliverables?

[09:25] Marcus Lee: Sure: 1) run full 2k token bench (cold/warm) and post p50/p95/p99 by 2026-04-22, 2) run quantization experiments and post quality deltas by 2026-04-28, 3) sample reranker test early next week. I'll attach example outputs and a short readme.
[09:55] Tom Rivera: That timeline works on our side for the bench. We'll upload eval and prompt sets by EOD.

[10:03] Elena Park: I'll send the pricing scenarios and a short doc describing the routing and fallback playbook by 2026-04-23. Andre will share the role mapping and onboarding runbook in the shared folder now.
[10:20] Andre Gomes: sharing now — folder link: drive.company.com/brightline-pilot (note: internal link placeholder).
[10:32] Priya Shah: One ask for the next call — could you include a short demo of the console showing token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency? That will help ops signoff.
[10:45] Elena Park: Absolutely, we'll demo the console next week and show the p95 drilldowns. Any final questions?
[11:00] Miguel Santos: No more from me. please include the SOC2 doc and network diagram in the same folder so procurement can kick off the review.
[11:12] Elena Park: Will do. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the items and cadence for the canary plan. Meeting adjourned.
[41:50] (call ends)
